title: Junk Drawer Organization Ideas: Keep the Drawer, Lose the Chaos
description: You don't have to get rid of the junk drawer. A 15-minute junk drawer cleanout plus 6 Amazon finds so you can find the scissors on the first try.
intro:
Every home has one. The drawer with batteries (dead or alive, who knows), takeout menus from 2019, three dried-up pens, a mystery key and somehow a single birthday candle.

Here's the good news: you don't need to get rid of the junk drawer. Honestly, it's one of the most ADHD-friendly ideas ever invented. One place for all the small, random, useful stuff? Yes, please.

The problem isn't the drawer. It's that everything is jumbled, so finding anything means digging. Let's fix that in about 15 minutes.

sections.heading: Step 1: Dump it all out (2 minutes)
sections.body:
Take the whole drawer out if it slides out, and dump it on a towel on the counter. Wipe out the crumbs while it's empty.

Seeing everything at once is what makes this fast. Trying to sort inside the drawer is how we end up holding a rubber band for ten minutes.

sections.heading: Step 2: Toss the obvious stuff (3 minutes)
sections.body:
Grab a trash bag and go fast:

- Dried-up pens and markers
- Expired coupons and old menus (they're all online)
- Broken anything
- Twist ties from bread you ate months ago
- Keys you can't identify (tape them together in a bag labeled "mystery keys" if letting go feels scary)

Don't overthink it. If you didn't even know it was in there, you won't miss it.

sections.heading: Step 3: Make groups (5 minutes)
sections.body:
Group what's left into little piles. Most junk drawers boil down to the same groups:

- **Write:** pens, a marker, sticky notes
- **Fix:** small screwdriver, tape measure, tape
- **Power:** batteries, a charger, a small flashlight
- **Cut and stick:** scissors, tape, glue stick
- **Random but useful:** rubber bands, birthday candles, a lighter

Five or six groups is plenty. If something doesn't fit any group, ask if it belongs somewhere else in the house.

sections.heading: Step 4: Give each group a box (5 minutes)
sections.body:
This is where the magic happens. Small drawer dividers or a set of mix-and-match trays turn the jumble into little rooms. Each group gets its own box.

When everything has a box, you can see what you have at a glance. And putting things back is easy because there's an obvious spot.

sections.heading: Keep it working
sections.body:
- **One in, one out:** if the drawer is full, something leaves before something new goes in.
- **Monthly dump:** first of the month, take 5 minutes to toss trash and re-sort. Put it in your calendar.
- **Overflow lives elsewhere:** spare batteries go in a battery case in the closet. The junk drawer only holds the ones you use often.

The drawer will get messy again. That's fine. With boxes in place, a reset takes minutes, not an afternoon.

finds.why: Different sizes snap together to fit your drawer, so every group of stuff gets its own little room.

finds.why: Test a battery in two seconds and store spares by size. No more guessing which ones are dead.

finds.name: Small magnetic strip for scissors and tools

finds.why: Stick it inside a cabinet door to keep scissors and a screwdriver visible and grabbable.

finds.name: Expandable drawer divider
finds.why: Splits a deep drawer into lanes so taller stuff stays upright and findable.

outro:
The junk drawer isn't a failure. It's a smart system that needed a few walls. Give it boxes and it'll give you the scissors on the first try.

For more 15-minute fixes like this, *The Messy Brain Home Reset* has a whole week of them, one small zone a day.
